JSON: Name: llha_net_pipeline Title: Layer-by-layer hierarchical attention network (LLHA-Net) for robust two-view correspondence outlier removal and pose estimation Short Hypothesis: Integrating a layer-by-layer channel fusion module (LLF), a hierarchical attention module (HA) and a permutation-invariant 1×1 convolutional block (PIHA) into an iterative correspondence pruning network increases outlier-removal F1 score by at least 3 percentage points on the YFCC100M known-scene test set compared with a T-Net baseline trained under identical conditions. Related Work: Existing two-view correspondence methods follow three families: geometric hypothesis verification (e.g., randomized sampling consensus methods), point-cloud/point-set neural classifiers (e.g., PointNet/PointNet++ variants and context-normalization based networks), and attention/transformer based feature matching and refinement. Random-sampling methods are robust but computationally intensive and sensitive to sampling. Point-set networks capture local/global cues but often ignore hierarchical multi-stage feature fusion and struggle with permutation-invariance on sparse correspondence sets. Attention and transformer-based matchers provide strong global context but typically operate at a single scale, are detector-dependent or detector-free without explicit outlier-specific fusion, and may be memory or compute heavy. Prior neural pruning networks incorporate iterative refinement or channel attention but either fuse only the final stage features or use fixed fusion weights, which reduces robustness when inliers are rare. Open limitations are (1) loss of per-stage semantic information during multi-stage fusion, (2) insufficient combination of global perceptual and structural local semantics across levels, and (3) lack of permutation-invariant processing for unordered sparse correspondence inputs. Abstract: We present a structured research pipeline for LLHA-Net, an iterative two-view correspondence learning architecture that combines layer-by-layer channel fusion with hierarchical attention and a permutation-invariant attention block to improve outlier removal and camera-pose estimation. The pipeline formalizes a network that (1) preserves and aggregates per-stage channel semantics via a layer-by-layer fusion (LLF) module, (2) extracts and adaptively fuses global perceptual and structural semantic cues via a hierarchical attention (HA) module, and (3) enforces permutation invariance for sparse unordered correspondence inputs using a 1×1 convolutional PIHA wrapper. The main contribution is the design and experimental evaluation plan to quantify how staged channel preservation and multi-level attention improve precision and F1 for outlier rejection and downstream pose accuracy. Expected outcomes include statistically significant gains in precision and F1 for outlier removal and improved mean average pose accuracy (mAP) at common angular thresholds compared to state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating improved robustness when inlier ratios are low. Experiments: Datasets: 1) YFCC100M two-view subset: use same sequences as prior work; split known scenes for training/validation/testing (60/20/20) and hold out specified unknown sequences (e.g., Buckingham Palace, Sacre Coeur, Reichstag, Notre Dame) for generalization tests. 2) SUN3D indoor: split 239 known scenes for train/val/test (60/20/20) and hold out 15 scenes as unknown. 3) 3DMatch for point-cloud registration (train on train set, test on 1623 test pairs). 4) Remote sensing registration dataset with diverse urban/natural scenes for qualitative verification. Baselines: RANSAC, PointNet++, CNe-Net, DFE, OA-Net, T-Net, PESA, MSA-Net, and optionally SuperGlue/LoFTR for descriptor-level comparisons. Metrics: For outlier removal: Precision, Recall, F1 on correspondence labels. For pose estimation: mean average precision (mAP) at rotation/translation thresholds 5° and 20°; report with and without RANSAC-weighted postprocessing. For registration: rotation error (deg), translation error (m), registration recall at predefined thresholds, and 3D registration RMSE. Experimental protocol: Train all neural baselines and LLHA-Net from scratch where applicable with Adam optimizer, batch size 32, initial learning rate 1e-4, mixed-precision on NVIDIA A100/3090 GPUs; use weighted loss: classification cross-entropy plus essential-matrix regression loss; set alpha schedule to 0 for first 2k iterations then 0.1 for remaining iterations (match original schedule). Report mean and standard deviation over 3 independent runs with different seeds. Ablations and comparisons: (A) Full LLHA-Net vs T-Net (architectural extension). (B) Module ablation: remove/replace LLF, HA, PIHA individually and in combinations to measure delta P/R/F and mAP. (C) Channel fusion variants: LLF vs PointCN and LLF+LLF vs PointCN+PointCN combinations. (D) Pooling variants in HA: GAP vs GMP. (E) PIHA vs PCSE (permutation-equivariant squeeze-and-excitation) comparison. (F) Iteration count: 1 vs 3 vs 5 iterative stages. (G) Postprocessing: with and without standard RANSAC refinement. Logging and evaluation: save checkpoints every epoch, evaluate on validation set, run final evaluation on known and unknown scenes and report full metrics in tables and precision-recall curves. Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Overfitting and label imbalance: heavy fusion may overfit to training scenes where inlier distributions differ; rare inlier ratios can bias classifiers toward low-recall solutions. 2) Misclassification trade-offs: aggressive channel fusion and attention weighting can increase precision at the cost of recall, harming downstream completeness for reconstruction. 3) Permutation-invariance sensitivity: relying on 1×1 convolutions for invariance assumes exchangeability of correspondences; structured dependencies beyond exchangeability may be under-modeled. 4) Compute and memory: iterative multi-stage fusion and attention modules increase parameters and GPU memory, limiting deployment on low-resource devices and realtime systems. 5) Dataset and evaluation bias: results may be dataset-specific (YFCC100M, SUN3D) and not generalize to extreme domains (very low texture, large illumination changes, non-rigid scenes). 6) Dependence on pre-extracted features: method assumes reliable keypoints/descriptors; failures in detection or descriptor extraction propagate downstream. 7) Evaluation coupling with RANSAC: reported pose gains may rely on downstream RANSAC; without RANSAC improvements may be smaller. 8) Scalability: runtime grows with number of correspondences and attention costs, limiting large-scale image-pair processing.
